name: Neon World 3

runtime.layout: Original scene meshes and wooden floor are retained; runtime fills missing furniture with a king-size upholstered bed, companion bedside table, two-seat sofa, reading chair, sliding wardrobe, lounge table, brass floor lamp, indoor plant, curtains, ceramic vase and digital wall clock. The existing TV/console and source nightstand/pillows are reused when present; furniture is measured for room bounds and collision clearance at load
runtime.lighting: Smooth local-time lighting transitions through dawn, fajr, sunrise, morning, noon, afternoon, sunset, maghrib, evening and night; a procedural skyline is visible through the window and the sun disc is limited to sunrise/sunset. Uses the device clock/time zone without requesting geolocation; one soft shadow-casting key light and fill/rim lights are adjusted at runtime

license.permission_note: User confirmed permission to use this asset in Aether.

warnings: Unity shaders, Udon scripts and VRC components were omitted; baked lighting and reflection probes are approximated with runtime lights.
The web-ready GLB does not expose every furniture prefab under a usable runtime name. Missing named items are supplied by local procedural Three.js furniture; source meshes are kept where available.
The bed is sized as a realistic king-size sleeping surface, seated on the wood floor and arranged with a matching side table, wall clock and candle.
The TV is kept upright with measured clearance above the console when that original console is present; a simple framed display is generated only if the TV root is missing.
The imported LedCircle renders as a misplaced arc protruding above the wall clock and is hidden at runtime; the separate Carpet mesh is also hidden to reveal the continuous wooden floor.
The digital clock uses the device's local 24-hour clock. Sky and lighting phases follow the same local time zone; no location data is requested and no live weather service is queried.

The web scene provides one measured bed-approach interaction point and validates furniture bounds/collision clearance. Unity collider/spawn-point counts remain unverified; there is no complete room navmesh, sit/sleep pose, or movable door/drawer rig in the current source scene.
